subject: Deployment mode selection & migration plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration plan

Hi Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant and patient-facing summarization (latency < 400ms 95th for short prompts).
- Current stack: prototyped against OpenAI API; production inference today runs on a small on-prem GPU cluster (4x A100) managed by infra team.
- Requirements: PHI-presence in prompts, VPC networking, audit logs (SOC2), and predictable monthly unit economics as usage ramps.
- Migration priority: minimize query drops during cutover; want options for staged migration (mirror traffic -> canary -> cutover).

Deployment modes we discussed:
1) Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, minimal infra ops, Redwood-managed keys and infra. Good if data residency and strict VPC controls are not mandatory.
2) Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (SLA-backed), predictable throughput and cost, good middle ground if you need isolation but still want managed servicing.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking and keys (KMS/HSM), required for regulated PHI workflows or air-gapped environments.

Recommended next steps:
- Can you confirm whether Nova Health requires the private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workflows, or whether Dedicated with VPC peering would suffice?
- I'll attach the migration checklist and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines for mirror/canary phases.
- If Dedicated or Private, will procurement require a SOW or standard contract? If you can share the procurement contact, we'll include procurement-friendly artifacts.

Attachments: 2026-06-18-call-notes.pdf (call notes), redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (ballpark pricing).

Happy to jump on a follow-up with your infra lead to map cutover steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

1) We prefer starting with Dedicated + VPC peering rather than hosted. Main reasons: (a) compliance/legal wants more control, (b) predictable monthly cost helps budgeting.
2) We have an on-prem cluster used for some legacy batch jobs; we do not want to run the production inference there long-term — mainly for latency/cost reasons — but we may want a hybrid during migration.
3) Can you share a sample network diagram for Dedicated with VPC peering and the required firewall rules? Priya would like to review.

Next steps from Nova Health: Priya to provide procurement contact and a short list of compliance questions (SOC2 scope, data retention, audit logs). Can Redwood share SOC2 evidence and an example MAP that includes mirror/canary traffic setup?

Hey team — quick sizing note: based on 1.2M tokens/day (mixed short/medium prompts) and latency target ~400ms 95th, recommended starting configuration: Dedicated pool of 4x H100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale headroom + burst to handle peaks. That gives consistent latency and headroom for canary/mirror traffic. We can simulate traffic patterns during the MAP to validate.

On the dedicated vs private trade-offs: 
- Dedicated + VPC peering typically meets security controls for most healthcare customers if paired with customer-side firewall rules and KMS key access controls.
- Private on-prem is recommended only if legal requires full-key custody or air-gap; it increases operational lead time (2-6 weeks for infra setup) and a slightly higher baseline cost.

I'll draft a short technical note and the network diagram Marissa requested. Happy to jump on a call with Priya next week to walk through the firewall rules.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
